newsitem.title: UK: US insurance body urges Supreme Court on liability.
newsitem.headline: US insurance body urges Supreme Court on liability.

text.p: The American Insurance Association has urged the U.S. Supreme Court to reverse a ruling that it says could lead to an explosion of liability lawsuits based merely on the fear of a future injury
"The decision threatens to turn liability law on its head," said Craig Berrington, AIA senior vice president and general counsel in a statement on Tuesday.

"Tort history underscores one requirement that has been a constant over time and jurisdictions: plaintiffs must suffer a real injury or be placed in imminent and immediate physical danger. In this instance, there was never any threat of immediate injury," he said.
The row emerged in the case of Metro-North Commuter Railroad versus Michael Buckley, a railroad worker exposed to asbestos who has not yet sustained an injury.
A 1994 ruling in another case created a 'zone of danger' benchmark that recognised that liability for negligent infliction of emotional distress includes near misses as well as direct hits.

"But the Court did not expand liability to include plaintiffs who were never at risk of suffering a direct hit. The zone of danger test limits recovery to emotional trauma caused by nearly suffering a physical calamity," Berrington said in the statement.
He added that if the lower court ruling is upheld, it could create a flood of litigation based upon the fear of future injury.

"Trying to predict how courts and juries would decide to compensate such potentially open-ended claims might even jeopardise the ready availability of liability insurance for certain types of risks," he said.

Berrington concluded: "Courts and insurers do not and cannot reasonably be required to compensate all who fear that they might suffer an injury in the future, irrespective of whether they actually do so. We urge the Supreme Court to reverse this decision."
The American Insurance Association is a trade association based in Washington D.C. representing more than 300 major insurance companies which provide all lines of property-casualty insurance.
